Q: Amazon Sagemaker - AttributeError: module 'sagemaker' has no attribute 'LinearLearner' A:

It seems you have installed version 3.x but you try to run code for 2.x

You may check it with pip show sagemaker

And you may have to install it as pip install "sagemaker<3"

You may see some differences in SageMaker V3 Release

Q: SA_RESETHAND flag in sigaction not working for swift exceptions A:

Regarding SIGILL and SIGTRAP, specifically, Apple replied to my report (FB16389781) referencing the POSIX documentation for sigaction noting SA_RESETHAND isn't supported for these signals:

SIGILL and SIGTRAP cannot be automatically reset when delivered; the system silently enforces this restriction.

Q: Error [ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED]: Cannot call write after a stream was destroyed while running a email reading code A:

It seems that the server you’re connecting to has a self signed cert which causes the connection to close, removing your ability to write. You will need to add the CA as a trusted root, or set the following env variable NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0. The second option is highly discouraged as it will allow all certs to be accepted.

Q: Do I need install php5-mysql A:

No — you don’t need php5-mysql.

Since you’re on PHP 7, just install the matching package:

sudo apt-get install php7.0-mysql
sudo systemctl restart php7.0-fpm nginx

That will fix the error.

Q: Using replace function in select with join A:

Both the queries are almost same in terms of performance. In the first query sorting is done twice, once when you are selecting the distinct records and again when it is performing an inner join, and in the end a merge join is there to select the final result set. Whereas in second query sorting is done only once but Hash join is being performed which is more expensive then merge join. So both the queries are same performance wise in the scenario when you don't have any index on the table.

Q: Where is the Project Directory in Microsoft Visual Studio? A:

Usually a Visual Studio project directory is a sub-directory of a solution directory. However, it doesn't need to be. E.g. you can add a project to multiple solutions.

For any given project, in the project settings the location of the project directory is available via the $(ProjectDir) macro expansion.

You can also use such macro expansions to access ordinary environment variables.

The difference between #include "blah" and #include <blah> is that the former adds a compiler-dependent additional search for the header, before (if that fails) doing the same search as the latter. With most (all?) modern compilers the additional search includes searching in the directory of the including file. Thus,

one way to add a file so that you can write just #include "myfile" in your code, is to place the file in the same directory as the including code.

Q: How to detect the OS from a Bash script? A:

I just care about Windows and Linux (specifically: Linux Ubuntu), but I want more information about them than is provided by the main answer here.

So, here's my extension of the main answer to provide more details about which version of Linux or Windows you are running:

terminal_check.sh:

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Gabriel Staples
# Sep. 2025
# See: https://stackoverflow.com/a/78480875/4561887


# Linux terminal
if [[ "$OSTYPE" == "linux-gnu"* ]]; then
    OPERATING_SYSTEM="Linux: $(lsb_release -d | cut -f2-)"

    # There is a bunch of OS-specific stuff for Ubuntu inside the 
    # `/etc/os-release` file. You can check for a specific version 
    # of Ubuntu like this: 
    . /etc/os-release
    if [ "$VERSION_ID" == "22.04" ]; then
        echo "You are using Ubuntu 22.04!"
    fi
# MSYS2: Git Bash terminal ~v2.44 and earlier
elif [[ "$OSTYPE" == "msys" ]]; then 
    OPERATING_SYSTEM="Windows: MSYS2: Git Bash terminal $MSYSTEM: $(uname -a)"
# MSYS2: Normal MSYS2 terminal, or Git Bash terminal ~v2.45 and later
elif [[ "$OSTYPE" == "cygwin" ]]; then 
    OPERATING_SYSTEM="Windows: MSYS2: Cygwin terminal $MSYSTEM: $(uname -a)"
fi

echo "OPERATING_SYSTEM = $OPERATING_SYSTEM"

Example output from a Bash terminal on Linux Ubuntu 22.04:

OPERATING_SYSTEM = Linux: Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS

Example output when run in Git Bash (from Git For Windows) on Windows:

OPERATING_SYSTEM = Windows: MSYS2: Git Bash terminal MINGW64: MINGW64_NT-10.0-22631 S-C0356 3.4.7-25de8b84.x86_64 2023-08-28 21:32 UTC x86_64 Msys

Example output when run in the ucrt64 terminal in MSYS2 on Windows:

OPERATING_SYSTEM = Windows: MSYS2: Cygwin terminal UCRT64: MINGW64_NT-10.0-22631 S-C0356 3.6.4-23a25d49.x86_64 2025-07-16 16:15 UTC x86_64 Msys
